model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; GAAP earnings after regulatory capital retention, preferred stock deducted in the equity bridge, net debt zero)

equity_bridge.item: Preferred stock (Series C, E, F; liquidation value)
equity_bridge.note: 1,400,000 preferred shares at $1,000 liquidation = $1,400m at 30 Sep 2026 (Q3 2026 10-Q note 6: Series C 500, E 400, F 500; carrying value $1,369m). Dividends ~$81m/yr (nine months 2026 $61m). Deducted at liquidation value because the flows are total net income before preferred dividends.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 1.1% vs EPS 5yr 17.5%: book value is depressed by AOCI swings (-3.3bn at FY2022 from AFS marks) and ~$5bn of buybacks since 2018, while FY2020 EPS (1.03) is a COVID-provisioning trough that flatters the 5yr EPS CAGR. Neither is a forward growth rate; revenue CAGR is used.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue = NII + noninterest income from XBRL 10-K tags: FY2015 5,378; FY2020 6,287; FY2022 7,215; FY2025 7,526. FY2022-23 revenue was inflated by the rate cycle (FY2023 NII 5,320 peak) then fell back as deposit costs re-priced; the 3yr CAGR (1.4%) is measured from that elevated base. FCF CAGRs are null: operating cash flow is meaningless for a bank. Diluted shares fell 963m (FY2021) -> 857m (Q2 2026), so per-share growth runs ~2pp/yr ahead of aggregate growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Regions grows revenue ~4% for two years as its fixed-rate asset book and hedges reprice and the Southeast footprint keeps adding loans and low-cost deposits, then tapers to nominal-GDP-like 2.5%. Efficiency drifts from ~57% to ~56%, credit normalises to a ~45bp mid-cycle loss rate, and roughly 80% of earnings are distributed through the dividend and buybacks while CET1 is held near 10%. Valued as FCFE at a 10% cost of equity with preferred deducted.
scenario_narratives.bull: Southeast in-migration and share gains from smaller banks lift loan growth to ~5%, a steeper curve pushes NIM toward the high 3s, and fee lines (wealth, capital markets, treasury management) compound at ~7%. Positive operating leverage takes the efficiency ratio to ~54% with benign credit, so pre-tax margins exceed 40% and buybacks keep shrinking the share count.
scenario_narratives.bear: Fed cuts compress NIM on an asset-sensitive balance sheet while a CRE (office, multifamily) and consumer credit cycle in the Southeast takes provisions to ~11% of revenue in FY28. Revenue shrinks, regulators push for capital rebuild and AOCI recognition under the Basel III endgame re-proposal, and distributions are cut. Recovery leaves a slightly lower through-cycle margin and 2% terminal growth.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on what it can pay its shareholders: net income less the capital it must retain to keep growing at its regulatory ratio, capitalised at the cost of equity. Deposits and wholesale funding are the raw material of the business, not debt to be subtracted. Regions earns a mid-to-high-teens return on tangible common equity on a granular Southeast deposit franchise; at ~2.2x reported tangible book (~1.7x ex-AOCI) the market already prices most of that.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: Southeast CRE and consumer losses could take provisions to 2-3x mid-cycle (FY2020 provision was 21% of revenue); Q3 2026 charge-offs of 29bp are near cycle lows.
Rate path: Fed cuts compress NIM on an asset-sensitive balance sheet; deposit betas on the way down may lag.
Basel III endgame / AOCI: recognising the ~$3.2bn after-tax AOCI loss (up from $1.9bn at June 2026) in CET1 would cut excess capital and buybacks.

Deposit flight: 2023 regional-bank stress showed uninsured-deposit runs can force balance-sheet repositioning losses; deposits fell $1.6bn in nine months 2026 while borrowings rose $5.6bn to fund loan growth.
FY0 still contains one estimated quarter (Q4 2026); refresh on the FY2026 10-K and FY2027 guidance in January-February 2027.

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E total revenue = net interest income + noninterest income (GAAP, not FTE). FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026 and is unreported, so FY0 = nine months 2026 actual 5,753 (NII 3,823 + noninterest income 1,930; Q3 2026 10-Q income statement) + Q4 2026 at ~1,977 (Q3 2026 actual 1,973 = NII 1,298 + fees 675, held roughly flat: NIM 3.68% already at the ~3.7% exit rate guided, capital-markets income at a record that is not extrapolated). FY2025 actual 7,526 (NII 4,991 + fees 2,535), so FY0 is +2.7%. Using FY2026E as FY0 puts year 1 = FY2027. The CSV `Revenue` column (FY2016-FY2021 ~58-104, blank thereafter) is an ASC-606 fee subset tag and is NOT bank revenue; every revenue figure here comes from the NII + noninterest income lines.
inputs.share_count_basis: 849.8m common shares outstanding at 30 Sep 2026 (Q3 2026 10-Q balance sheet: 890,784,135 issued less 41,032,676 treasury) PLUS ~4m dilutive restricted/performance awards (Q3 2026 diluted weighted average 856m vs 852m basic) = ~854m fully diluted. Held FLAT thereafter: share-based compensation (~$70m/yr) is expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count; buybacks ($95m in Q3 2026, ~3m shares) are a distribution of the FCFE capitalised, not a separate driver.
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. Regions is a Fed-regulated bank holding company: long-term borrowings $5,982m and short-term borrowings $4,500m at 30 Sep 2026 and deposits $129,510m are operating funding whose cost is already inside net interest income; cash and due from banks $2,867m plus interest-bearing deposits in banks $7,462m are liquidity held against that funding, not surplus. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (net income less capital retained to hold CET1 at target as risk-weighted assets grow) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash is added. total_debt and cash are recorded for audit only. Preferred stock ($1,400m liquidation value, $1,369m carrying; ~$81m/yr dividends) is senior to common and deducted in equity_bridge; the flows are therefore total net income BEFORE preferred dividends, so the preferred cost is charged exactly once.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE = GAAP net income ~2,355 (nine months 2026 actual 1,760; Q4 at ~595 = (1,977 revenue - ~1,125 noninterest expense - ~105 provision, i.e. above Q3's 68 as the 29bp charge-off rate is not extrapolated) x (1 - 20.5%)) LESS capital retained ~515 (~4% RWA growth x ~$12.8bn of CET1 required at a ~10% target; loans grew 95.6bn -> 99.8bn, +4.4%, in nine months). Cross-check on distributions: nine-month common dividends $684m + buybacks $555m = $1,239m; FY2026 ~$940m + ~$650m = ~$1.6bn, i.e. ~68% of GAAP NI, with CET1 rising to 10.84%. reported_fcf = FCFE + SBC so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 2,181; FY2024 1,598; Q3 2026 -15) is loan/deposit/trading movement and is meaningless as free cash flow for a bank; the CSV FreeCashFlow column is NOT used. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC charge.
inputs.sbc_source: us-gaap:AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense FY2025 $69m (10-K equity-award note; ShareBasedCompensation cash-flow tag not used by Regions); FY2024 $73m and FY2023 $61m (CSV StockBasedComp). Taxes withheld on net-share settlement (PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation) FY2025 $23m, nine months 2026 $26m are inside the expense already recognised and are not added again. ~0.9% of revenue, so house and street bases are close.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income IS the banking business, and no cash is added to equity value (matching-asset rule satisfied in the other direction).
inputs.buyback_note: Repurchases of common stock $555m in nine months 2026 ($401m Q1, $59m Q2, $95m Q3); FY2025 $1,067m, FY2024 $348m, FY2023 $252m. Diluted share count fell from 938m (FY2023) to 856m (Q3 2026), -8.7%. Quarterly dividend raised 13% to $0.30 in Q3 2026 (40-50% payout target). Buybacks are a use of the FCFE capitalised, not an extra source of value.
inputs.book_value_anchors: 30 Sep 2026: shareholders' equity 17,847 - preferred 1,369 - goodwill 5,748 - other intangibles 120 = tangible common equity 10,610 -> TBVPS ~$12.49 on 849.8m shares (down from ~$13.63 at 30 Jun 2026). The fall is entirely AOCI: Q3 2026 other comprehensive loss was -1,275 (AFS securities -717, cash-flow hedges -582), taking AOCI to -3,197; ex-AOCI TBVPS ~$16.25, up from ~$15.89. CET1 excludes AOCI for a Category IV bank and rose to 10.84%. Nine-month 2026 ROTCE ~20% annualised on reported TCE (NI to common 1,699), ~16.5% ex-AOCI.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single cost of equity 10.0% across scenarios (risk is charged in the scenario cash flows, not twice through the rate): US 10-year ~4.3% + beta ~1.15 x 5.0% ERP = ~10.0%. USD flows, USD rate. Regional banks carry a premium to money-centre peers for deposit-run and CRE concentration risk (2023 precedent); that premium is in the beta. House precedent: HBAN 10.5% (merger-integration premium), NAB.AX 9.7%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Bank: operating-lease expense sits inside noninterest expense, which is inside the margin; no separate lease line.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity through the component engine route, per the dcf-methods routing row for banks and the house precedent for US/AU banks (HBAN, NTRS, NAB.AX, GL): an owner-FCF/WACC DCF is meaningless for a deposit-funded bank. Model UNCHANGED from the 2026-10-02 first valuation. Engine mapping: revenue = NII + noninterest income; 'ebitda_margin' = pre-tax income + SBC as % of revenue (i.e. 100 - efficiency ratio - provision ratio + SBC%); D&A = 0 (inside noninterest expense); 'capex' = capital retained to hold CET1 at target as RWA grow (~1.66 x revenue growth, from ~$12.8bn required CET1 / ~$7.73bn revenue); cash tax = GAAP effective rate. Preferred deducted in equity_bridge; net debt zero. UPDATE 2026-11-19 (Q3 2026 10-Q): anchors refreshed - price, share count (854m, unchanged after rounding), balance sheet to 30 Sep 2026, and the FY2026E revenue base 7,650 -> 7,730 on Q3 actuals (revenue 1,973, NIM 3.68%, efficiency 56.7%, NCO 29bp, net income 631). DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: every forward driver path in all three scenarios (growth, margin, capital retention, tax, cost of equity, terminal) and the 25/50/25 weights. Q3 2026 ran ahead of the FY27 base margin (nine-month pre-tax margin 38.6% vs 37.2% on the engine's pre-SBC basis) only because provision was 3.9% of revenue against a ~6% mid-cycle assumption; one quarter of 29bp charge-offs is not evidence the through-cycle loss rate has fallen. What would move them: FY2027 guidance (January 2027) for NII growth outside 3-5% or expense growth that breaks the 57% efficiency ratio; charge-offs holding under 35bp through 2027 (base provision path down); a final Basel III endgame rule that pulls AOCI into Category IV CET1 (bear retention path up, and with AOCI now -$3.2bn that risk is larger than at the prior valuation); a 10-year Treasury move of 50bp+ (cost of equity). Excess CET1 above target (10.84% at Q3 2026 vs a ~9.25-9.75% operating range) is NOT added as surplus capital - treated as a buffer against AOCI recognition, which at -$3.2bn after tax would cost ~2.5pp of CET1 if phased in fully. The Q3 2026 AOCI loss (-$1.3bn, AFS marks and receive-fixed hedge marks as rates rose) does not enter FCFE: it reverses as securities and swaps pull to par and signals higher reinvestment yields, but it is why reported TBV fell. RF_Analysis.json (Q3 2026 refresh) cross-checked: FY2026 guidance reaffirmed (low-single-digit loans and deposits, NIM exit ~3.7% achieved early, NCOs improving vs the 40-50bp range), Frazer Lanier acquisition closed July 2026 (record capital-markets quarter; immaterial to scale), dividend +13% to $0.30/quarter, 130-150 branch openings offset by closures (inside the efficiency path).

bear.growth_rationale: Rate cuts compress NIM (asset-sensitive deposit base reprices slower than floating loans) and a Southeast CRE/consumer credit cycle shrinks loan demand in FY27-28; recovery to 2-3% thereafter.
bear.margin_rationale: FY28 credit trough: provision ~11% of revenue (~90bp NCO plus reserve build, cf. FY2020 provision 1,330 = 21% of revenue in a severe case) on efficiency ~60% as revenue falls; mature 36.5 = efficiency 57.5 - provision 6.9 (higher through-cycle losses) + 0.9.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention above 1.66 x g in FY27-28 despite flat RWA: CET1 buffer rebuild through the credit cycle and Basel III endgame AOCI phase-in; then 1.66 x g.

base.growth_rationale: Total revenue. FY27 4.0%: average loans +3-4% (H1 2026 gross loans +3.7% annualised, Southeast footprint population growth), NII +3-4% as fixed-rate loans/securities and the hedging book reprice above roll-off yields, fees +5% (wealth, capital markets, treasury management). Tapers to 2.5% terminal (nominal GDP less deposit-beta creep). Brackets the 3.4-3.7% 5yr/10yr revenue CAGR.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax income + SBC on revenue = 100 - GAAP efficiency ratio - provision/revenue + SBC 0.9. FY27 38.1 = 100 - 57.0 efficiency - 5.8 provision + 0.9. FY2025 actual: efficiency 57.3% (4,313/7,526), provision 6.2% (470), pre-tax 36.4%. H1 2026: efficiency 57.9%, provision 4.2% (reserve release; NCOs 232 = 6.1% of revenue), pre-tax 37.9%. Mature 38.9 = efficiency 56.0 (modest positive operating leverage, technology spend absorbed) - mid-cycle provision 6.0 (~45bp NCO on ~$100bn loans) + 0.9. UPDATE 2026-11-19: path unchanged. Nine months 2026 actual: efficiency 57.5% (3,307/5,753), provision 3.9% (227), pre-tax 38.6%; Q3 alone 56.7% / 3.4% / 39.9%. The beat is provision running below mid-cycle, which the path already normalises back to ~6%. UPDATE 2026-11-19: path unchanged. Nine months 2026 actual: efficiency 57.5% (3,307/5,753), provision 3.9% (227), pre-tax 38.6%; Q3 alone 56.7% / 3.4% / 39.9%. The beat is provision running below mid-cycle, which the path already normalises back to ~6%.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold CET1 at ~10% as RWA grow with revenue = growth x required CET1 (~$12.8bn) / revenue (~$7.73bn) = ~1.66 x g. FY27-28 at 4% growth: 6.6% of revenue (~$525m, ~22% of NPAT retained -> ~78% distributed, consistent with the ~$905m dividend + ~$0.9bn buybacks pattern of FY2025). Steps down with growth to 4.2% at the 2.5% terminal rate (~15% retained).
base.tax_rationale: GAAP effective rate: FY2025 21.4% (587/2,743), nine months 2026 20.7% (459/2,219), Q3 2026 19.8%; 21% federal + state less tax-exempt income and LIHTC credits. Held at 21%: the sub-21% prints rely on tax-credit investment volume that is not capitalised in perpetuity.

bull.growth_rationale: Southeast deposit/loan share gains plus a steeper curve lifting NIM toward ~3.7%; fees +7% on wealth and capital-markets build-out.
bull.margin_rationale: Efficiency ratio improves to ~54% (positive operating leverage of 2-3pp/yr as revenue outruns ~3% expense growth); provision holds ~5.5% (benign credit, ~40bp NCO); + SBC 0.9.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = 1.66 x revenue growth, as base; faster growth consumes more capital.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default, matching the bank precedents (NTRS, HBAN): regional banks carry fat-tailed credit and deposit-flight risk (2023), RF's earnings are rate-sensitive in both directions, and the Basel III endgame AOCI treatment is unresolved. No solvency risk is in view (CET1 ~10.5-11%, $130bn deposits largely retail/core), so bear is not overweighted.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
